subject: SparrowAI dedicated capacity: SKU mix recommendation and ops notes
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@sparrowai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SparrowAI dedicated capacity: initial fit questions

Hi Emily — great to meet yesterday. To drive a concrete Dedicated SKU mix for SparrowAI I have a couple quick clarifying questions so we can size a guarded reserve pool and a recommended fallback/hedge strategy. High level what we heard: ~50 sustained requests/sec (text gen + reranking), peak bursts to ~150 rps, heavy long-context use (12k-32k tokens for a subset of customers), and a target latency SLO of p95 < 650ms for the interactive flows. Correct?

Specifics that matter for SKU tradeoffs:
- Typical sequence lengths for the long-context models (average generation length vs max)
- Percent of workload that is single-turn low-latency (embeddings, short replies) vs long multi-turn generation
- Any requirement for on-prem/VPC-only model variants or encryption/HSM constraints that affect quantized kernels

I sketched an initial hypothesis: use a small H100 pool (for 80GB long-context variants), an A100 pool for mid-memory fine-tuned models, and a larger L4 pool for low-latency single-turn and embeddings. I can turn this into a day-by-day cost/throughput delta & a fallback playbook if you confirm the workload split.

Attaching a lightweight workbook with a couple simulation knobs (batching, prefix cache hit) — I’ll follow up internally and share a recommended guarded-reserve plan by Tuesday.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sparrow_dedicated_sku_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), latency-throughput-sims.csv (csv)
From: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@sparrowai.com>

Date: 2027-06-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SparrowAI dedicated capacity: initial fit questions

Thanks Ethan — correct on the high level. A few clarifications:
- Long-context: we have two model families. Family A is 40–60k token retrieval-augmented models used in batch workflows but also in interactive sessions (~10% of requests). Family B is interactive long-session agents where typical context is 12–20k and generation is 1–2k tokens (about 20% of requests).
- Short-turn: ~60% of requests are short (single-turn Q&A or embeddings) — these need <200ms p95.
- Peak and throughput: sustained 50 rps now, expect 2x growth over next 12 months. Bursts often align with business hours in US-EAST region.
- Security: we need customer-managed keys (KMS) and SSO; we will want Private deployment for the Dedicated plan but the runtime must support quantized kernels if we choose to use 4-bit formats for cost reasons.

Budget: initial committed spend for Dedicated reserved capacity ~ $120k/month; we are flexible on mix if you show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Best,
Emily
Emily Stanton
Head of Platform, SparrowAI
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-13T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SparrowAI dedicated capacity: initial fit questions — internal sizing discussion

Folks — Emily’s note below with the workload split. Quick internal read: she needs both long-context headroom (Family A batch + Family B interactive) and a low-latency pool for 60% of traffic. Key constraints: KMS/HSM + Private deployment + support for quantized kernels. Budget ~ $120k/month commit.

My initial thinking (high level):
- H100 (80GB) x4 reserved: primary long-context pool for Family A & Family B hot paths. Reason: 80GB NVMe-backed HBM to keep KV cache for 40–60k contexts and to avoid aggressive tiling for Family A. Also gives best perf for fp16 and int8 heavier models.
- A100 (80GB) x6 reserved: mid-memory, good for fine-tuned variants and multi-turn where we can shard/tiling more aggressively but still need throughput.
- L4 (24GB equivalent) x18 reserved: low-latency front-end for single-turn Q&A, embeddings, and most API traffic. L4 gives much better cost-per-token for short contexts and fast warmup.

Operational notes / tradeoffs to call out for the proposal:
1) Memory headroom vs tiling: Family A’s 40–60k context will need either 80GB class GPUs or a tiling+KV-cache design that increases CPU/GPU orchestration complexity. Given Sparrow’s desire for Private with KMS, recommending H100 for headroom simplifies SLA and reduces operational fallthrough risk.
2) Quantization: L4/A100 are friendly for int8/4-bit quant; H100 supports better fp16 throughput and also has fp8 path on newer ISAs. If Sparrow wants maximal cost savings, a hybrid where Family B is quantized (with quality validation) on A100/L4 could reduce spend ~20–30%. But we must run evals.
3) Fallback policy: reserve enough A100 slots to accept overflow from H100 for non-interactive batch Family A jobs (with relaxed latency). Also propose preemptible burst pool (cloud-sourced) for non-critical batch pipelines to keep cost within $120k if committed pool is underutilized.
4) Autoscale/bursting: recommend conservative autoscale for L4 to handle short spikes, and strict admission control to protect H100 slots for long-context sessions.

Numbers: I ran quick sim knobs in the attached workbook (see tabs: "sims_v1" and "cost_model"). Under current traffic and 2x growth: the above mix keeps p95 latency targets for interactive flows within 450–600ms for L4/A100 and 700–900ms for worst-case Family A when served from H100 (with KV cache warm). Cost delta vs A100-heavy mix: ~+18% committed cost but much lower risk of tail latency and orchestration complexity.

Ben / Kim / Dev — thoughts on counts and whether A100 x6 is enough to act as hedges for H100 overflow? Also any ops concerns for Private + KMS + quant kernels?

Thanks,
Ethan

Date: 2027-06-15T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SparrowAI dedicated capacity: internal sizing discussion — proposed plan

Emily / team — following our internal sizing pass, here is a concise recommended plan that fits SparrowAI’s requirements and the $120k/mo commit. I’m including operational guardrails and next steps.

Proposed committed pool (initial, 12-month window):
- H100 80GB x3 reserved (primary headroom for Family A batch and Family B interactive hot sessions)
- A100 80GB x8 reserved (mid-tier for fine-tuned variants and overflow from H100; configured with quantized kernels where quality checks pass)
- L4 24GB-class x20 reserved (front-door for short-turn traffic and embeddings; autoscale to burstable capacity within budget)

Why this mix?
- Reduces committed cost vs Ethan’s conservative H100 x4 while preserving long-context headroom. Dropping to 3 H100s assumes good KV cache hit behavior and acceptance of occasional tiling for the coldest Family A workloads (we'll queue or offload to batch preemptible pool).
- Adding an extra A100 slot provides a larger overflow buffer and better throughput for multi-turn fine-tuned variants while still enabling quantized cost savings.
- Larger L4 pool ensures the p95 <200ms for single-turn flows under 2x growth and allows short-lived request bursting without touching expensive H100 slots.

Operational guardrails:
- Admission control: tag sessions by model-family. Only sessions marked Family A long-batch take H100; Family B interactive prefer H100 but fall back to A100 with degraded latency SLA (we'll surface via headers).
- KV cache policy: keep a hot-set on H100 for top 10% customers; implement prefix caching on L4 for short-turn paraphrase cache.
- Quantization rollout: run an eval ramp for Family B on A100 & L4 with quality gates (BLEU/ROUGE + targeted human spot checks).
- Fallback & burst: preemptible cloud pool for batch jobs + elastic L4 autoscale.

Estimated committed cost (mid-case): $112k/mo committed (hardware + basic support) with an expected additional $8–12k/mo in burst/ops buffer depending on utilization. This keeps them inside the $120k target and allows us to add H100 slot if adoption of Family A exceeds projections.

Next steps:
1) Emily: confirm willingness to accept H100 x3 + A100 x8 + L4 x20 in contract draft (we can model alternate pricing for H100 x4 if you prefer more headroom).
2) Dev / Kim: prepare a short runbook for Private deployment KMS integration + quant kernel validation windows.
3) Ethan: schedule a 30-min review with Sparrow for Wednesday to walk through simulations and attach the workbook with tuned knobs.

Emily — happy to answer questions or iterate. If you’re comfortable, we’ll convert this to the formal MOQ and begin procurement/ops planning.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
